topic: TrajPack: Local-First Observable Agent Trajectory ETL and Compliance Router

key_points: Local-first agent workspace: sessions, settings, and run records stay on the machine by default
'Log is the Runtime': model messages, tool calls, tool results, and termination facts enter an append-only Runtime Event Log; sessions, UI, model context, and recovery are projections over that log
Event-sourcing architecture: one execution authority (Runtime Host) owns session, turn, agent lifecycle, tools, and events
Context is not history: tool-result pruning and LLM compaction change what the next inference sees without discarding recorded evidence
Decision audit trail + persistent memory for AI trading agents
Tamper-evident SHA-256 chain with RFC 3161 timestamp anchoring for verifiable records
Cites MiFID II Article 17 (algorithmic decision documentation) and EU AI Act Article 14 (systematic logging of AI actions) as compliance drivers
20 MCP tools; outcome-weighted recall so agents learn from every trade
Evidence layer for AI agents: audit trails, approvals, policy gates, compliance reports for every action
Signs every action with ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204, quantum-safe) and produces regulator-ready audit trails
Policy enforcement before execution; works with LangChain, CrewAI, MCP
Targets EU AI Act and DORA compliance
AI observability platform for production LLM and agent systems
Built on OpenTelemetry: traces, metrics, logging for LLM and agent workloads
Focus on debugging, monitoring, and evaluating agents in production
Economical human-readable logs and structural (event pattern) retrieval for agentic trajectories
Emphasizes cost-efficient logging and queryable event patterns rather than raw token dumps

stats.fact: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions define dedicated agent spans (create_agent, invoke_agent, plan, execute_tool) with gen_ai.operation.name and gen_ai.provider.name attributes, giving a vendor-neutral schema for trajectory telemetry.
EU AI Act Article 12 (Record-Keeping) requires high-risk AI systems to automatically record events (logs) enabling traceability of the system's functioning across its lifecycle.
EU AI Act Article 14 (Human Oversight) requires systematic logging of AI actions so human oversight is possible; Article 17 (Quality Management) mandates documentation and record-keeping.
MiFID II Article 17 raises the bar for algorithmic decision documentation in financial trading, requiring firms to record and explain algorithmic decisions.

Apache Maka (Incubating, ~2k stars) demonstrates the local-first append-only event-log pattern: model messages, tool calls, tool results, permission decisions, and termination events recorded as recoverable execution facts.
Asqav signs agent actions with ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204, quantum-safe) to produce tamper-evident, regulator-ready audit trails for EU AI Act and DORA.

angles: Local-first vs hosted-first: keep trajectory data on-prem for privacy, sovereignty, and compliance while still shipping to a router/warehouse
Event-sourcing as the backbone: append-only log as the single source of truth, with projections for UI, context, and recovery
Compliance router: route trajectory events to the right destination (retention, redaction, warehouse, audit store) based on policy
Tamper-evidence: SHA-256 chaining + RFC 3161 timestamp anchoring + quantum-safe signatures (ML-DSA/FIPS 204) for regulator-ready audit trails
OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions as the standard schema for agent spans and tool spans
Cost-efficient ETL: human-readable logs and structural event-pattern retrieval instead of raw token dumps
